Solve the following geometry problem. Give the exact numerical answer and explain your reasoning in English. You have no access to tools.

In an acute scalene triangle ABC, let M be the midpoint of BC and K the foot from A to BC. Suppose BC=16, AM=10, AK=8, and BK>KC. Choose D1,D2 on BC with BD1=6 and BD2=9. For i=1,2, let Ui be the intersection other than A of circle ABDi with line AC, and Vi the intersection other than A of circle ACDi with line AB. Let Zi be the center of circle AUiVi. Find Z1Z2.

Solve the following geometry problem. Give the exact numerical answer and explain your reasoning in English. You have no access to tools.

Let O and H be the circumcenter and orthocenter of an acute scalene triangle ABC, with OH=6. At A, let Ka and La be where the internal and external angle bisectors meet line BC, respectively, and let Ma be the midpoint of BC. Let Pa be the intersection other than A of circle AKaLa with line AMa. Define Pb and Pc cyclically at B and C. Let Z be the center of circle PaPbPc. Find OZ. Assume all circles and intersections are nondegenerate.

Two circles tangent to line PQ at P and Q intersect at A and B on the same side of PQ, with B closer to PQ than A. Triangle APQ is acute and scalene. Reflect B across PQ to obtain C. If AP=6, AC=3*sqrt(34)/2, and tan(angle BAQ)=3/5, find the area of triangle APC.

A convex quadrilateral ABCD satisfies 0<angle ABC=angle ADC<90 degrees. The internal angle bisectors at B and D meet AC at E and F, and P=BE∩DF. Let M be the midpoint of AC. Circle BPD meets the interiors of segments BM and DM again at X and Y, respectively (other than B and D). Let Q=XE∩YF and let V be the foot from P to AC. Points P,Q lie on the same side of AC, with Q farther from AC. If PM=sqrt(29)/2, PV=5/2, and QM=sqrt(101), find PQ.

Choose a common tangent to ω and circle BOC on whose same side the centers J,U lie, and let its points of tangency be Y and Z, respectively. Find YZ.

In an acute triangle ABC with AC>AB, let Γ be the circumcircle and O the circumcenter. The tangent to Γ at A meets line BC at P, and X is the foot from A to line OP. Choose unique points E on line AB and F on line AC, both on the A-side of line OP, such that angle EXP=angle ACX and angle FXO=angle ABX. Line EF meets Γ at K,L; let σ be the circumcircle of triangle KLX with center U. Point P lies outside σ. Ray PU meets σ at Y,Z in that order, nearer first. If PY=3 and YZ=9, find PX.
